x.role: Codex & ChatGPT @OpenAI
x.summary: OpenAI 核心开发者 Thibault Sottiaux 宣布开启为期 28 天的“极简与提效”冲刺计划，专注于简化产品逻辑、提升运行效率及引入突破性功能。同时，他展示了利用 AI Agent（Dot）实现“收件箱清零”的自动化工作流，并确认 GPT-6.1 Sol 的性能已恢复正常。
x.translation:
在接下来的 28 天里，我们每天要么发布一项对大多数 Codex/工作用户有明显改进且相关的功能，要么进行一次全面重置。改进计划现在开始。

好了，我们开始锁定目标。目前唯一的工作重心是：简化、提升效率以支持更多使用场景、开发突破性功能或引入新模型。

有时你必须超前投资，但用户的反馈很明确：大家都希望产品变得更简单。我们正在处理。

它所做的事情：
- 删除所有我不需要保留的邮件类别，并批量验证；
- 识别我工作类型的标签，并为所有邮件贴上适当的标签；
- 指导我处理需要回复的邮件，并在后台搜索相关背景信息以确保回复准确。
在此过程中，我处理了人们直接通过电子邮件发送给我的大量反馈和请求。这是一个充实的周六。

我这辈子从未实现过“收件箱清零”，直到我把它设定为我的 Dot（AI 助手）的一个主动目标。看看能维持多久，但这感觉真棒。

幸运的是，我们未来的模型在代码删除和简化方面会做得更好。正好赶上。

全部修复。没想到这里有这么多 Pro 500 用户。

收到一些报告称 Pro 500 没有像预期的那样进行重置。正在调查并将进行补偿。

未读邮件从刚才的 9000 多封减少到了 6110 封。我将在 48 小时内通过干净的过滤器实现收件箱清零。Dot 已经接受了这个挑战。

你可以让你的 Dot “创建一个宠物并将其设置为你的头像”。它可以基于一个想法、一张图片或几乎任何东西。这是我的 Dot。

全球重置将于太平洋标准时间明天上午 10 点面向所有付费 ChatGPT 账户上线。对于 GPT-6.1 Sol 的缓慢启动表示歉意，在经历了前两天的巨大负载激增后，它现在已恢复到预期的运行速度。
x.recommendation: Thibault 的动态揭示了 AI 产品从“功能堆砌”向“极简主义”转型的趋势，对于 AI 从业者而言，如何利用 Agent 自动化处理繁琐的日常工作（如收件箱管理）是极具参考价值的效率范式。此外，其 28 天高频迭代的策略展示了在模型性能波动期如何通过快速响应和重置来重建用户信任。

As models speed up (as with Astra 𝚞𝚕𝚝𝚛𝚊𝚏𝚊𝚜𝚝), harness overhead matters more and more.

DHH is fundamentally right about Rust. For context, Vercel has been undergoing a Rust-ification (carcinization, technically 🦀) for a while.

One of the first projects we migrated was Turborepo, from Go to Rust¹. The migration completed, but the RoI was actually quite controversial internally.

While Rust was in our eyes better for low-level OS access, something crucial for a build system like Turbo, the human migration costs were very sustantive.

Go is very fast. It's beautifully designed. It's easy to iterate on. We were very conflicted about the migration, because it was *humans* writing the code, *even if we knew Rust was a better choice*.

The calculus has now changed. What's "best for humans" is no longer necessarily "best for business". 

FWIW, it's also quite unlikely that Rust is the end-all-be-all toolchain. I'm quite certain there's greener pasture ahead, because Rust itself was designed before the 'supersonic tsunami' of agents hit.

x.author: Aaron Levie
x.role: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
x.summary: Box CEO Aaron Levie 指出，AI 正在重塑企业就业结构，催生了“自动化工程师（FDE）”等全新岗位。他强调，AI Agent 的大规模落地仍处于早期阶段，企业需通过重构工作流、升级治理与安全体系，才能释放百倍于现状的生产力。
x.translation:
【推文 1】我们已经开始看到 AI 正在创造哪些新工作。AI 的经济部署需要大量的技术工作和配套服务，这意味着 AI 工程师（构建企业级应用 AI 产品）、负责将 Agent 部署到公司内部的 FDE（全栈部署工程师）以及新兴 AI 服务公司的岗位需求激增。目前的就业统计数据甚至低估了企业内部向 AI 转型的工作岗位，许多原有的数据、研究和软件岗位正在被重新定位。银行、生命科学、制造甚至律师事务所都在引入技术人才或调整现有角色，以协助 Agent 部署。在 AI 真正发生前，人们很难想象它创造了什么，而现在我们正见证这一过程。

【推文 2】这一指标（指 AI 使用率）可能更多反映了消费级 AI 的商业模式，而非 AI 的真实水平。消费级 AI 几乎不可避免地会通过商业、广告或设备及服务购买进行补贴和变现，该指标的增长可能会比我们预期的更早趋于平缓。

【推文 3】AI Agent 的采用目前呈现明显的双峰分布：编码及相关任务已起飞，而其他领域尚处早期。即便在编码领域，采用模式也差异巨大，从后台并行 Agent 到 1:1 交互不等。而在知识工作领域，真正的 Agent 采用仍处于起步阶段，因为大多数工作流需要重构，包括数据重组、责任归属、治理合规及安全升级等。目前我们所见的仅是冰山一角，未来 Agent 的采用率有望实现百倍增长。

【推文 4】我接触的大多数企业都在推行一个大趋势：在各部门部署内部 FDE，以弥合 AI 能力与底层工作流之间的鸿沟。这需要极高的技术专长、AI 理解力以及对业务流程的洞察。自动化没有捷径。这是一个全新的企业职能，将创造大量就业。正如每一代技术都会创造前所未有的岗位，‘自动化工程师’正是这一代的关键角色。如果你有软件背景并正在钻研 AI，这是一个值得深耕的领域。
x.recommendation: Levie 揭示了 AI 落地从“聊天机器人”向“工作流重构”的范式转移。对于 AI 从业者，关注“自动化工程师（FDE）”这一新兴角色，以及企业在合规、治理和流程重构上的痛点，是捕捉下一波企业级 AI 红利的关键。

rawTweets.text:
We’re already starting to see what kind of new jobs AI is creating. 

AI requires significant technical work and surrounding services to deploy into the economy. This means jobs for AI engineers that build applied AI products sold to (or within) enterprises, FDEs to deploy agents into companies, new services firms for deploying AI, and more. 

And even the published stats of new jobs undercount all the existing jobs that are transitioning to new areas of AI work in an enterprise. Many prior data, research, and software jobs large enterprises are also being repositioned for working with AI. 

Every bank, life sciences company, manufacturer, and even law firm is bringing on more technical talent -or repositioning existing roles- to help with agent deployment in their companies. It’s a lot easier to picture what AI can replace vs. what it creates until it starts happening. Now we’re seeing what this looks like.

This metric may tell us more about the business model of consumer AI than the state of AI. AI for consumers almost inevitably will be subsidized and monetized via commerce, ads, or purchases of devices and other services. This metric may level off lower than we think. https://t.co/HGKoWJGHci

AI agent adoption is still very bimodal right now. You have coding and coding adjacent tasks which have taken off, and then everything else. 

And even within coding, you have a very wide continuum of adoption patterns, with some likely a small percentage of developers deploying background agents working on projects in parallel, and the rest of everyone else still working with agents 1:1. 

Then, there’s the entire rest of knowledge work where real agentic adoption is still very early. The reason for this is that most of the workflows still need to reengineered to work with agents. 

This isn’t the same as deploying a chat system for better research efficiency, but instead requires workflows to be rebuilt, data to be wired up in new ways, new practices for accountability and liability of decisions when agents are in the mix, governance and compliance paradigm changes, security upgrades, and more. 

We’re still so unbelievably early in what this is going to look like outside of a few categories of work right now. This is why you can basically expect 100X more agent adoption from what we’ve seen so far.

A big trend with most enterprises that I talk to is deploying internal FDEs into departments in their organization to help bridge the capabilities of AI into their underlying workflows. 

This requires a high level of technical expertise, an understanding of AI, and the ability to understand the workflows and processes that the enterprise is trying to automate. There’s no shortcut to getting automation without this combination of skills (either in one person or multiple). 

What’s exciting is this is an entirely new function in most enterprises, which is going to create a ton of new roles in the economy.

“Every generation of technology creates jobs that didn't exist before it, jobs that arise from an immediate need in an emergent industry. The Automation Engineer is a key example of those jobs for this generation. Nobody has ten years of experience doing this yet, because ten years ago the tools that made it possible didn't exist (it didn’t even exist two years ago).”

If you have software skills and are diving into AI, this is an area to go deep on.

（推文 3）趋向平均值。当每个人都在盯着别人看以决定自己该做什么时，我们最终会停止创造属于自己的东西。我们复制那些有效的东西，借用语言、审美和功能。我们称之为“向市场学习”、“遵循最佳实践”、“保持竞争力”。结果，一切都变得似曾相识：精致、可互换，没有错，但也毫无生命力。平均值本身并不坏，但它是我们消除所有“差异化理由”后的终点。数字比感受更容易比较，所以我们制造那些能产生数字的东西。我们研究什么能获得关注，然后把自己塑造成那个样子。最终，反馈不再是工作的参考，而是工作的作者。我们不再问自己想表达什么，而是问什么会被奖励。AI 让这个循环变得毫无阻力。它能借鉴的参考比我们一生能看到的还要多，但拥有所有视角并不等同于拥有一个属于自己的视角。它没有经历过那种让某个细节变得难以忍受或无比美丽的独特人生。当我们要求它替我们做选择，却不带入任何个人意图时，我们得到的就是一种看似合理、容易通过的东西。然后我们发布它、衡量它、复制它，并将其反馈到下一轮。一场平庸的浪潮。这不仅改变了工作，也改变了工作的人。我们用平台能分发、市场能理解的类别来描述自己：设计师、创始人、创作者。选一个细分领域，建立品牌，保持一致。那些不符合的部分变得碍手碍脚，即使正是这些矛盾可能产生我们最有趣的作品。我们变得更容易被分类，也更难被区分。我认为我们需要像艺术家一样去创造。艺术家通过作品发展出一种视角：创作、观察、选择、失败、回归。学习那些即使没人关心也依然重要的东西。技艺赋予了这种视角一种足够精确的形式，让别人能够体验。工作之外的生活也很重要。你住过的地方、爱过的人、那些你羞于启齿却在乎的事。这些不是干扰，而是你拥有表达欲望的源泉。在音乐、绘画、摄影、电影中我们理解这一点。我们期待在选择中看到“人”的存在。我们想体验一些没有他们就无法遇见的东西。软件也可以做到这一点。一段软件表达了对生活应有的感受、什么值得关注、什么应该自由改变、任务是该像文书工作还是游戏。即使是一个微小的交互，也能承载某人的关怀、幽默或好奇心。但我们很少把软件当作一种媒介来谈论。我们把它当作一个产业：要占领的市场、要优化的工作流、要追赶的竞争对手。我们添加功能是因为别人有，而不问它是否属于这里。产品堆砌着相同的零件，失去了让它们值得被选择的灵魂。在品牌包装之下，一切都一样。艺术家也会向他人学习。问题在于，你是将这些影响吸收进自己的观点中，还是用它们来逃避建立观点？你试图让别人感受、理解或做什么？为什么是这种特定的形式？你注意到了哪些现有工具似乎没注意到的东西？这些问题没有可以从竞争对手路线图中借来的答案。如果我们几乎可以制造任何东西，决定“什么值得存在”就变得比以往任何时候都重要。速度给了我们更多行使判断力的机会，它并没有消除责任。我不想要一个每个人都成为相同思想的高效分发者的世界。我希望人们利用这些工具深入挖掘他们真正关心的东西。让事物变得足够具体，以至于我们能感受到背后的人。如果每个人都能制造东西，但最终大家制造的都是一样的东西，那又有什么意义呢？
（推文 4）翻盖手机，完整桌面。一个小小的世界。iPhone Duo 上的 ryOS。
x.recommendation: Ryo Lu 的思考直击 AI 时代软件开发的痛点：工具的易用性导致了创造力的平庸化。对于 AI 从业者而言，这篇长文是一剂清醒剂，提醒我们在追求效率和模型能力的同时，不要丢掉软件作为“表达媒介”的灵魂，以及作为创造者应有的独特审美与立场。

convergence to the mean

when everyone looks at everyone else to decide what to make, we eventually stop making anything of our own.

we copy what works. borrow the language, the aesthetic, the features. we call it learning from the market, following best practices, staying competitive. together, everything starts to feel familiar. polished, interchangeable. nothing wrong. nothing alive.

the mean isn’t necessarily bad. it’s where everything lands when we remove the reasons for it to be different.

numbers are easier to compare than feelings, so we make things that produce numbers. we study what gets attention, then shape ourselves around it. eventually the feedback stops informing the work and starts authoring it. we’re no longer asking what we want to say. we’re asking what will be rewarded for saying.

ai makes this loop frictionless. it can draw from more references than we could see in a lifetime. but access to every perspective isn’t the same as having one. it hasn’t lived a particular life that makes one detail unbearable and another beautiful. when we ask it to choose for us without bringing any intention of our own, we get something plausible, easy to approve.

then we ship it, measure it, copy it, and feed it back into the next round. a tidal wave of mid.

this changes not just the work, but the people making it.

we describe ourselves in categories platforms can distribute and markets understand. designer. founder. creator. pick a niche. build a brand. be consistent. the parts that don’t fit become inconvenient, even when those contradictions might produce our most interesting work. we become easier to classify and harder to tell apart.

i think we need to approach making things more like artists.

an artist develops a perspective through the work. making, noticing, choosing, failing, returning. learning what matters even when nobody else cares. craft gives that perspective a form precise enough for someone else to experience.

the life outside the work matters too. the places you’ve lived, the people you’ve loved, the things you’re embarrassed to care about. these aren’t distractions from having something to say. they’re how you come to have something to say.

we understand this with music, paintings, photographs, movies. we expect a person to be present in the choices. we want to experience something we wouldn’t have encountered without them.

software can do this too.

a piece of software expresses beliefs about how life should feel. what deserves your attention. what you should be free to change. whether a task should feel like paperwork or play. even a small interaction can carry someone’s care, humor, or curiosity.

but we rarely talk about software as a medium. we talk about it as an industry. markets to capture, workflows to optimize, competitors to catch up with. we add a feature because someone else has it, without asking whether it belongs. products accumulate the same parts and lose what made them worth choosing.

underneath the branding, it’s all the same thing.

artists learn from others too. the question is whether you’re absorbing those influences into a point of view, or using them to avoid developing one.

what are you trying to let someone feel, understand, or do? why this particular shape? what have you noticed that the existing tools don’t seem to notice?

those questions don’t have answers you can borrow from a competitor’s roadmap.

if we can make almost anything, deciding what deserves to exist becomes more important, not less. speed gives us more chances to exercise judgment. it doesn’t remove the responsibility.

i don’t want a world where every person becomes a more efficient distributor of the same ideas. i want people to use these tools to go further into what they actually care about. to make things specific enough that we can feel someone behind them.

what is the point of everyone being able to make something, if we all end up making the same thing?

x.author: Andrej Karpathy
x.summary: Andrej Karpathy 近期分享了关于 LLM 输出评估与交互形式的深刻见解。他展示了通过地理坐标测试模型对世界的“压缩式理解”，并提出从文本转向交互式网页、图表及定制化视频的未来交互范式。
x.translation:
【推文 1】很酷的评估方法。只需给 LLM 提供经纬度坐标，并询问“陆地还是水域？”。重复 16,200 次并绘制成图。模型确实懂，这源于它们对互联网数据的压缩。

【推文 2】未来我们将花更多时间去理解语言模型的输出。以下是一些心得与技巧：

写作方面：我发现让 LLM 使用 ASD-STE100（一种最初为航空航天维护文档开发的受控语言规范）来解释事物非常有效。LLM 对此非常精通，且该规范对简洁文风有严格限制，可读性极高。有时我会要求“80% 的 ASD-STE100 程度”，因为原规范过于严苛。

图表/图像：比起纯文本，让 LLM 生成图表更易于处理和理解。

网页：要求输出“HTML 格式”以获得精美的交互式网页。LLM 在前端开发方面进步神速，能创造出美观的体验和动画。

解释性视频：我最看好的是针对任意主题生成完全定制化的解释视频。尝试指令如“创建一个 3b1b 风格的 X 主题解释视频，并使用我的 ElevenLabs API 密钥进行配音”。这已经开始奏效了！

总结：
- 随着 LLM 能力提升，它们将自主完成更多繁重工作，人类的工作重心将上升到监督与理解层面。
- 幸运的是，LLM 本身就能辅助这一过程。随着智能与代码变得廉价，你可以要求生成大型、定制化且“一次性”的软件制品（如网页应用、视频），这在过去是不可想象的。大胆尝试，你会感到惊喜。

We'll be spending a lot more time trying to understand the outputs of language models. A few thoughts, tips & tricks:

Writing. Something I've had success with: Ask your LLM to explain something in ASD-STE100, it's a controlled language specification originally developed for aerospace maintenance documentation. LLMs well-versed in this language and it comes with heavy constraints on clean writing style that I often find a lot more readable. Sometimes I've tried to soften it a bit e.g. ask for "80% of the way to ASD-STE100" because the spec is quite stringent. But even better:

Diagrams / images. Instead of writing, ask your LLM to create a diagram. These can be a lot easier to process, parse, and understand. But even better:

Web pages. Ask for output "in HTML" to get a beautiful, interactive webpage. LLMs are getting really good at frontend and can create beautiful experiences, animations, etc. But even better:

Explainer videos. The output format I am most bullish on is fully custom / bespoke explainer videos generated on any arbitrary topic. Experiment with things like "Create a 3b1b style video explainer on X. Use my ElevenLabs API key for audio narration". (you'd need an API key for the latter or you can ask your LLM to find you decent free alternatives that use your local compute). This is actually starting to work!

In summary:
- As LLMs get better, they will do more and more of the legwork autonomously, and a lot more of our work will rise up the abstractions into oversight and understanding.
- Luckily, LLMs can help here too because as intelligence and code are increasingly abundant, you can ask for large, custom, discardable software artifacts (e.g. web apps, video explainers) that would have never made sense to create before. Push the boundaries here and you'll be surprised.

blogs.title: An update on recent Claude Code quality reports
blogs.summary: Anthropic 近期针对 Claude Code 用户反馈的性能下降问题进行了深入复盘。调查发现，问题源于三个独立的技术变更：一是将默认推理强度从“高”降为“中”导致模型能力受损；二是会话清理逻辑的 Bug 导致模型出现重复性遗忘；三是系统提示词优化过度导致代码质量下降。目前所有问题已于 4 月 20 日修复，Anthropic 承诺将改进内部评估机制，并为受影响用户重置使用限额。
blogs.translation: 过去一个月，我们调查了关于 Claude 响应质量下降的反馈。经排查，API 层未受影响，问题集中在 Claude Code、SDK 及 Cowork 工具中。具体包括：3 月 4 日调整默认推理强度导致性能下降；3 月 26 日会话清理逻辑 Bug 导致模型表现“健忘”；4 月 16 日系统提示词调整导致代码质量受损。目前上述问题均已修复，我们正通过改进评估流程来防止此类事件再次发生。
blogs.recommendation: 该文展示了在 AI 产品中平衡“推理延迟”与“模型质量”的复杂性，对研发团队如何建立更灵敏的线上性能监控及用户反馈闭环具有极高的参考价值。

blogs.title: Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands

blogs.translation: Anthropic 推出 Claude 托管智能体，通过将智能体的大脑（模型）与手（执行环境）解耦，构建了长期运行的智能体服务。该系统将智能体虚拟化为会话、控制回路和沙箱三个独立组件，确保底层实现变更时接口保持稳定。这种设计借鉴了操作系统对硬件的抽象，避免了将智能体组件强耦合在单一容器中导致的“宠物式”维护困境，从而使系统能够适应模型能力的快速迭代。
blogs.recommendation: 该架构为构建复杂 AI 应用提供了极佳的范式，特别适合需要长期运行、高可靠性的智能体系统。建议研发团队参考其“组件解耦”设计，避免将业务逻辑与执行环境强绑定，从而降低模型升级带来的维护成本。

podcasts.title: Re-Founding Incumbents for the AI Era with Sequence Holdings Co-Founder and CEO Michael Lee

podcasts.title: Frontier Chips for Frontier AI Labs, with Walter Goodwin, Founder/CEO of Fractile
podcasts.summary: 本期播客探讨了AI算力竞赛的底层逻辑：在英伟达统治的GPU生态外，Fractile正通过全栈式芯片设计，试图通过内存带宽优化实现推理速度的质变。核心Takeaway：AI芯片的竞争本质是“推理时间算力（Test-time compute）”的博弈，谁能通过架构创新获得3-6个月的性能领先，谁就能主导未来的模型部署。反直觉洞见在于，目前的AI芯片市场存在严重的同质化，而真正的护城河并非单纯的算力堆叠，而是如何将AlphaGo式的“推理时搜索”能力高效植入大语言模型。精彩金句：“在芯片领域，如果你能结构性地创造出3到6个月的领先优势，你就赢得了所有的部署机会。”
podcasts.translation: Fractile创始人Walter Goodwin分享了公司愿景：构建专为超大规模模型设计的极速推理芯片。他指出，当前AI芯片行业存在严重的“同质化”倾向，而Fractile专注于解决内存带宽瓶颈，旨在将推理速度提升至新量级。他强调了“推理时算力”的重要性，即通过更强大的芯片支持模型在运行阶段进行深度思考与搜索，从而实现超越当前基准的性能表现。
podcasts.recommendation: 如果你关注AI硬件基础设施的未来演进，或者想了解除了英伟达之外，芯片初创公司如何通过差异化架构在巨头夹缝中寻找生存空间，这期节目不容错过。

githubTrending.recommendation: 随着 Agent 落地场景复杂化，行为可控性成为刚需，该项目今日激增近 300 Star 反映了开发者对 AI 安全与审计工具的迫切需求，值得关注。
